paper.title: Adaptive Exploration in Linear Contextual Bandit

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed contextual linear bandit with M discrete contexts
unmapped: Finite set of M contexts drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution p with p(m)>0; each context m has a known action set A^m of size K
settings.definition_quote: We consider the stochastic $K$-armed contextual linear bandit with a horizon of $n$ rounds and $M$ possible contexts. ... For each context $m \in [M]$ there is a known feature/action set $\cA^m\subset \mathbb R^d$ with $|\cA^m| = K$. ... $(\eta_t)_{t=1}^n$ is a sequence of independent standard Gaussian random variables ... we assume each $\cA^{m}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$ and $\|x\|_2\leq1$

unmapped: Finite set of M contexts drawn i.i.d. from an unknown distribution p with p(m)>0; known action sets A^m
Optimal arm unique for each context
settings.definition_quote: Assume that $p(m) > 0$ for all $m \in [M]$ and that $x_m^*$ is uniquely defined for each context $m$ and let $\pi$ be consistent.

symbols.C_lin: C(theta, A^1,...,A^M): optimal value of inf sum alpha_{x,m} Delta_x^m s.t. ||x||^2_{(sum alpha xx^T)^{-1}} <= (Delta_x^m)^2/2

conditions: optimal arm x_m^* unique for each context

source.label: thm:lower_bound
source.quote: Under the same conditions as \cref{lemma:confidence_width}, \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi}(n)}{\log(n)}\geq \cC(\theta,\cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M), where $\cC$ is defined as the optimal value of the following optimisation problem: \inf_{\alpha_{x,m}\in[0, \infty]}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{x\in\cA^m}\alpha_{x,m}\Delta_x^m subject to ...

results.notes: Regret is E[sum <x*_{c_t},theta> - Y_t], i.e. pseudo-regret against per-context optimal arm. C does not depend on context distribution. Equals 0 when optimal arms span R^d.

symbols.C_lin: C(theta, A^1,...,A^M): value of the lower-bound optimisation problem of Theorem 3

conditions: T_x^m(Delta) uniquely defined and continuous at Delta for all m, x

source.label: thm:upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $T_x^m(\Delta)$ is uniquely defined and $T_x^m(\cdot)$ is continuous at $\Delta$ for all contexts $m$ and actions $x \in \cA^m$. Then the policy $\pi_{\text{oam}}$ proposed in Algorithm \ref{alg:main} with $\epsilon_t = 1/\log(\log(t))$ satisfies \limsup_{n\to \infty}\frac{R_{\theta}^{\pi_{\text{oam}}}(n)}{\log (n)}\leq \cC(\theta, \cA^1,\ldots, \cA^M).

results.notes: f_n depends on n so horizon known. Solves a convex program per round (CVXPY), considered polynomial. Paper notes continuity follows from uniqueness (Lemma 27). Implies sub-logarithmic regret when optimal arms span R^d.

source.label: thm:ucb
source.quote: Consider the policy $\pi$ that plays optimistically by X_t = \argmax_{x \in \cA^{c_t}} \ip{\hat \theta_{t-1}, x} + \|x\|_{G_t^{-1}} \beta_t^{1/2}. Suppose that $\theta$ is such that $\{x_1^*, \ldots, x_M^*\}$ spans $\mathbb R^d$. Then, for suitable $(\beta_t)_{t=1}^n$ with $\beta_t = O(d \log(t))$, it holds that $\limsup_{n\to\infty} R_\theta^\pi(n) < \infty$.

results.notes: Bounded regret statement (limsup finite) encoded as O(1); constant is instance dependent and unspecified.

cited_results.setting_description: Classical K-armed bandit with unit-variance Gaussian rewards (special case M=1, A = standard basis), consistent policies
